brief:
Tonight is Pull B, and it is a light night — day three of the deload week that runs through Sunday 27 September. Meso 3, the next hard block, starts Monday 28 September.

Last night you ran the card as written and were out in 28 minutes with nothing to say about it. Same method tonight: the weights come off what you actually logged on 15 September, your own rep numbers stay, and the cut you feel comes from doing fewer sets. Nothing tonight should feel like work — every set should leave you sure you had four more in you.

The numbers. Bent-over row 125 for 9, two sets, down from 155 for 8. Close-grip pulldown 77 for 10, two sets. Straight-arm pulldown 8 kg for 10, two sets. Shrugs the 27.5 kg bells for 15, two sets. Curl one set of 12 on the 15 kg EZ bar. Reverse curl 27 for 10, two sets. Face pulls 27 for 13, one set.

Two of those are deliberately not a fifth off, and you should know which before you are standing in front of them. The close-grip pulldown is an eighth off, not a fifth: 77 is 12.5% below the 88 you finished on, and the only settings that machine has ever shown in your log are 77, 83, 88 and 93. A true fifth would be 70.4, and there is no evidence a 70 exists on that stack. I would rather give you a pin you can actually select and tell you it is a smaller cut than the label claims. The face pulls I am not deloading at all — same 27 you have done twice without a murmur. Dropping a light rear-delt set to 21 takes away shoulder work without shedding any fatigue, and it is already cut from two sets to one.

Two slots tonight are booby-trapped and it is not your fault. The curl slot has held two completely different things: 25 lb dumbbells in each hand through 3 September, then a 20 kg EZ bar in both hands on the 15th. The 15 kg bar I am asking for only makes sense if you pick up a bar — if you grab dumbbells instead, ignore the number and take something you can do twelve easy reps with. Same warning on the straight-arm pulldown: on 3 September that slot holds a machine for the first set and the cable crossover for the other two, at completely different weights. If you start on the machine tonight, 8 kg means nothing and you should pick your own light setting.

One correction from me. Last night's card told you to stop the dips at 12 and you did 8. You were right and the card was wrong: the 15, 17, 19 I based that on was logged as dips from a bench, and last night you were on the bars. Every set of bar dips in your log sits between 7 and 14 reps. Eight was a normal set, not a bad one.

One Yes/No card is waiting, about the shrug. You told me on 15 September that 35 kg is the heaviest dumbbell in the building, and you did fifteen reps with it on every set — the top of what the program asks for. So that lift has nowhere left to go in either direction going into Meso 3. The card asks to open the top of the rep range to twenty. It changes nothing tonight either way.

Off the floor, two things I keep asking for and have not got. Nobody has weighed you since 23 August — 207 lb, thirty-one days ago — and the show is 159 days out with the prep block written into the assessment week of 2 November. Prep steers by that number and it is blank. And your log still holds exactly one cardio session ever: 15 minutes on an elliptical, 21 July. The plan asks for two to three easy sessions a week during build blocks, and Meso 3 starts in five days. This is the cheapest week in the calendar to start both.

flags.note: Deload week, day 3 of 7 — runs through Sunday 27 September. Meso 3 starts Monday 28 September.

Two weights tonight are on purpose not a fifth off. The close-grip pulldown is 12.5% off your 88, because 77, 83, 88 and 93 are the only settings that machine has ever shown in your log and a true fifth (70.4) is not one of them. The face pulls are not cut at all — only their set count is.

Left alone the app would have cut far harder than the week's label says: 60 lb on a close-grip pulldown you finished at 88 (a 32% cut under a "-20%" sign), 32% off the straight-arm pulldown, 31% off the reverse curl, and every rep target dropped to the bottom of its range.

Three of tonight's lifts were logged on kg equipment but the app has them stored in pounds, so its own numbers would have printed 6.804 kg, 27.216 kg and 15.876 kg on the dial — none of which is a setting. Tonight's card is written in exact kg steps instead. The underlying fix is a code change I am not allowed to make.

The curl slot holds two different things across your log — 25 lb dumbbells in each hand through 3 September, a 20 kg EZ bar on the 15th. Tonight's 15 kg only applies if you take a bar. If you take dumbbells, pick your own weight for twelve easy reps.

Same fault on the straight-arm pulldown: on 3 September that one slot holds a machine for set one and the cable crossover for sets two and three, at different weights. If you start on the machine, tonight's 8 kg does not apply.

Correction to last night's card: it told you to stop the dips at 12, based on the 15, 17 and 19 you did on 14 September. That night is logged as dips from a bench and last night was dips on the bars — different exercise. Your 8 reps were a normal set for the bars, not a shortfall.

Your calf raise slot is carrying two different movements on two different scales: 240 lb machine sets, and 35, 40 and 45 lb logged on 17 September as kettlebell swings and thrusts. That is very likely what made the suggestion you complained about on 21 September look insane. It affects tomorrow's Legs B, not tonight, and the slot needs splitting in the exercise list — a code change, not a Yes/No card.

Tonight is your fifth straight training day. Your recovery trainer looked at it specifically and did not object: your plan runs six days on and one off, so the rest day is due on Friday 25 September, and the last two days were 27 and 28 minutes of deload work.

The one real fatigue mark in your log is 20 September, before the deload started: the same deadlift loads you pulled on 10 September gave you fewer reps (235 for 4 instead of 5, 255 for 3 and 3 instead of 4 and 4), under your own note that it was too early in the morning.

Your recovery trainer read all 32 notes in your log by hand and found no pain, tweak, pinch, strain, numbness or soreness anywhere. It reads them by hand because the automatic pain search is still broken — its only hit ever is your 23 August lateral-raise question, matched because "number" contains "numb".
The reverse curl is on the stall list — flat at 36 for four sessions. I am deliberately not chasing it this week. A stall is a Meso 3 decision and nothing gets chased inside a deload.

Two lifts on tonight's card are still named for equipment you do not use: the row says "Smith" and you row it with a barbell, and the curl says "Incline DB Curl" and you logged it as an EZ bar curl. The exercise list holds 37 entries and not one barbell or EZ-bar entry to swap them to. Code change, not a morning review.

No bodyweight since 23 August — 207 lb, thirty-one days ago — with the show 159 days out and the prep block written into the assessment week of 2 November. Prep steers by that number and it is currently blank.
Your log holds one cardio session ever: 15 minutes on an elliptical, 21 July. The plan asks for two to three easy sessions a week in build blocks, and Meso 3 starts in five days.

Three trainers reported. Five disagreements, each settled by taking one side whole: the recovery trainer won the close-grip pulldown, the reverse curl and the face pulls; the load trainer won the shrug and the curl. No vetoes, and no pain or injury objection from anyone.

proposals.why: You wrote that 35 kg is the heaviest dumbbell in the building on 15 September, and then shrugged it for fifteen reps on all three sets — the top of what this lift asks for, the same fifteens you hit on 3 September. The weight cannot go up and neither can the reps, so this lift has no way to get harder in Meso 3. This opens the top of the range to twenty. The bottom stays at twelve, so tonight's card is the same either way.

overrides.reason: 125 for 9, two sets, off the 155 for 8 you finished on 15 September. A true fifth off is 124 and you load this bar in 5 lb steps, so 125 is the bar that exists. Nine reps is your own number from that night — you did 9 at 120 and 9 at 140, and 125 sits between them. Both trainers landed here independently; it is the one lift tonight nobody argued about.

77 for 10, two sets. This is deliberately a smaller cut than the rest of the night: 77 is 12.5% below the 88 you finished on, not a fifth. The only settings this machine has ever shown in your log are 77, 83, 88 and 93, and 70.4 is not one of them — I will not print a pin I cannot show exists. You have started here twice, so two easy sets of ten off the lightest pin you use is the honest version, and the drop from three sets to two carries the rest.

8 kg for 10, two sets — an exact fifth off the 10 kg you did three times on 15 September, and a whole setting rather than something between notches. Both trainers agreed on it. Warning: on 3 September this one slot held a machine for the first set and the cable crossover for the next two, at different weights. If you start on the machine tonight, this number does not apply — take your own light setting.

The 27.5 kg bells for 15, two sets. A fifth off your 35s is exactly 28, but a 28 kg dumbbell appears nowhere in your log, while a 27.5 does — you rowed with one on 20 September. So 27.5 is the real bell and 28 was the arithmetic. Your own 15 reps stay; the third set is what the deload takes.

The 15 kg EZ bar for 12, one set. A fifth off the 20 kg bar is 16, but you have never logged a 16 — every kg weight in your log sits on a 2.5 step, so 15 is the bar that exists and it is a quarter off rather than a fifth. Twelve reps is your own number and it stays. If you take dumbbells instead of a bar tonight, ignore this weight entirely: this slot has held both, and 35 lb means nothing in each hand.

27 for 10, two sets — a quarter off the 36 you did for 10, 11 and 10 on 15 September. A true fifth would be 28.8, and 28 is a number I cannot show that stack has, while 27 is one you pinned as recently as 20 September. This lift is flagged stalled and I am leaving the stall alone: nothing gets chased inside a deload week.

27 for 13, one set — the same weight as usual, on purpose. This is the only slot tonight I am not deloading. You have done 27 for 13 twice with no complaint, on the 15th and again on the 20th, and a 21 lb face pull sheds no fatigue that 27 was creating. Cutting it would take away shoulder work for nothing. Going from two sets to one is the deload here.

dissent.progression: 70 for 10, twice — 0.8 x 88 is 70.4, a true fifth off his top set.
dissent.recovery: 77 for 10, twice — 77 is the lightest pin he has ever actually used on this machine; 70 is unproven.
dissent.why: The arithmetic is progression's and the machine is recovery's, and a card he cannot obey is worse than a cut that is smaller than advertised. The four settings this pulldown has ever shown in his log are 77, 83, 88 and 93 — spacings of six, five and five pounds, which is what a 2.5 kg stack looks like after conversion. 70 is not on that ladder; the notch below 77 would be about 71.6. Printing 70.4 is the exact fault that produced his complaint on 21 September — a number rounded to a grid the machine does not have. I took 77 and put the shortfall in writing on the card instead of hiding it: it is 12.5% off, not 20%, and the set cut from three to two carries the rest. Progression is not wrong about the fifth; it is wrong that the fifth is selectable.

dissent.progression: 27.5 kg for 15, twice — 28 is not a bell on a 2.5 kg rack, and he rowed with a 27.5 on 20 September.
dissent.recovery: 28 kg for 15, twice — an exact fifth off the 35 kg he named as the heaviest dumbbell in the building.
dissent.why: Same test as the pulldown, applied the other way round, which is how I know it is a test and not a preference: prescribe only a setting his log shows exists. A 27.5 kg dumbbell is in his log — he used one for rows three days ago. A 28 kg dumbbell is in no session he has ever recorded, and recovery's own note says his bells run 6, 7, 12.5, 15, 17.5 and 35 and that it cannot see the rack. Recovery then asks him to find the bell below 28 and report back, which is the panel handing him the decision it was convened to make. Half a kilo apart, and I am declaring it rather than letting a silent difference through.

dissent.progression: 15 kg bar for 12, one set — fixed bars step 15 then 17.5, and 16 kg is not one he has logged.
dissent.recovery: 16 kg bar for 12, one set — an exact fifth off the 20 kg bar he curled on 15 September.
dissent.why: Identical to the shrug and decided identically. Every kg figure anywhere in his log sits on a 2.5 step — 6, 7, 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15, 17.5, 20, 27.5, 35 — and 16 is not among them. 15 kg is a quarter off rather than a fifth, which is a slightly bigger cut than the week promises, and I am telling him that on the card. Both seats also independently flagged that this slot has held dumbbells and a bar at different times, so both prescriptions are void if he picks up dumbbells tonight; that warning is in the packet whichever weight won.

dissent.progression: 28 for 11, twice — 0.8 x 36 is 28.8, so 28 is the notch at or below it.
dissent.recovery: 27 for 10, twice — 27 is a cable setting he has actually pinned; 28 is not.
dissent.why: The same rule again, and this time it favours recovery. 27 appears in his log on 15 and 20 September on the face pulls and is a setting these cables demonstrably have. 28 appears nowhere. Progression itself wrote that 27 is the safe fallback and then prescribed 28 anyway. On the reps, recovery's 10 is his own opening number on this lift and progression's 11 is the middle of what he did; neither is wrong, but the winning side is taken whole, so it is 10. Both seats agree the stall gets left alone until Meso 3, and it does.

dissent.progression: 21 for 13, one set — 0.8 x 27 is 21.6 and 21 is a notch he used twice last night.
dissent.recovery: 27 for 13, one set — do not deload the only piece of shoulder-health work in the night.
dissent.why: This is the one place tonight where the brake argued for more weight than the load driver, and it is right. A face pull at 27 for 13 is not producing fatigue that 21 would relieve; he has done it twice in the last eight days without a word, and his all-time best on this lift is 45. The slot is already cut from two sets to one, which is the deload doing its work. Progression's 21 is arithmetically clean and achieves nothing — it would remove rear-delt and cuff work in a week whose purpose is to arrive at Meso 3 healthy. A rule applied where it does no good is just a rule.
